summary: Figure 5 illustrates how SWARM turns many sampled scenarios into one uncertainty-aware estimate. SWARM samples K demand matrices and has its CLPEstimator generate N routing samples for each, so every one of the resulting N×K traffic-and-routing samples has its own flow-completion-time (FCT) distribution, shown schematically as Scenario 1, 2 and 3's probability-vs-FCT curves. From each scenario curve, the 99th-percentile (99p) point is sampled out, indicated by a dashed purple arrow, and all three 99p values are pooled into a single composite distribution plotted at the bottom (probability vs. 99p FCT). The spread of this composite curve is what captures the uncertainty in SWARM's percentile estimate, which the paper notes can be reduced by increasing the number of samples. The figure is schematic: curve shapes, not real data, stand in for the general sampling-to-composite-distribution procedure.
